utterance:
Samuel, based on your symptoms—the pain starting around your belly button and moving to the lower right side, the loss of appetite, nausea, fever—and the tenderness I found when examining your tummy, I am very concerned that you have acute appendicitis, which is an inflamed appendix. 

You need to go straight to the hospital emergency department today so the surgical team can assess you, run blood tests and scans, and likely arrange an operation to remove your appendix before it bursts. How did you get to the clinic today—is someone here with you who can drive you straight to the emergency department?
reply: An operation? Can't I just get some antibiotics and go back to work?

utterance:
I understand it is a shock to hear you might need an operation, and I know you want to get back to work. However, appendicitis cannot be safely treated with tablet antibiotics at home. If an inflamed appendix is left untreated, it can burst (perforate) and cause a life-threatening infection throughout your abdomen called peritonitis. In the hospital, they will start intravenous antibiotics and fluids through a drip, give you strong pain relief, and the surgeons will talk you through the best treatment, which is usually keyhole surgery to remove the appendix.

It is really important that you do not eat or drink anything at all from now on—not even water—in case you need an operation under general anaesthetic today. Also, please do not drive yourself to the hospital. Have you got someone with you or nearby who can drive you straight to the emergency department now, or should we arrange an ambulance?
reply: Okay, I will get my mate to drive me over now.

awards.label: Refer to the emergency department today for surgical assessment
Phone the emergency department with a handover

utterance:
That sounds like a good plan. I have written a referral letter for you to take with you, and I have also called the emergency department to let them know you are on your way. 

To recap:
- Head straight to the hospital emergency department now with your mate driving you.
- Stay nil by mouth—do not eat or drink anything at all—so you are ready for surgery if needed.
- Do not take any anti-inflammatory painkillers like ibuprofen.
- If on the way or while waiting you start to feel dizzy, faint, have a sudden worsening of your pain, or start vomiting repeatedly, let the emergency triage staff know immediately or call 000 for an ambulance.

All the best Samuel, the team at the hospital will take good care of you.
reply: Cheers, Doc. I'll get going now.
